stories.headline: US politics live updates: King Charles addresses US Congress; Trump says Iran in ‘state of collapse’, wants Strait of Hormuz reopened
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the US Congress during his first state visit to the US, focusing on shared values between the two countries and praising NATO. The visit comes amid strained relations between the UK and US over the war in Iran. King Charles and Queen Camilla are on a four-day tour, visiting Washington, D.C., New York City, and Virginia. Meanwhile, former President Donald Trump stated that Iran is in a "state of collapse" and called for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The royal visit aims to strengthen ties between the two nations, with King Charles emphasizing the importance of their alliance and shared values, despite current tensions and disagreements, particularly over the Iran conflict. The visit is seen as an opportunity to reaffirm the US-UK relationship.

stories.headline: US politics LIVE updates: King Charles takes jab at Trump over White House renovations after historic Congress address; Trump administration moves to challenge Jimmy Kimmel's network licence
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the US Congress, navigating diplomatic issues with a subtle jab at former President Donald Trump over White House renovations. Meanwhile, the Trump administration is challenging ABC's network license due to a joke made by Jimmy Kimmel about Melania Trump. The FCC's review of ABC's license sets up a legal battle with Disney, ABC's parent company. This move comes after Melania Trump accused Kimmel of "hateful and violent rhetoric" and called for ABC to take action against him. The Trump administration's actions have sparked a potential conflict with the media company. The situation is unfolding amidst other developments, including a possible arrest warrant for James Comey and ongoing discussions on NATO, Ukraine, and climate change. King Charles's historic trip to the US has concluded, with politicians now tasked with building on the diplomatic efforts made during his visit.

stories.headline: Iran killed any delusions of US military domination over China
stories.summary: The US-Iran conflict has significant implications for the region and beyond. Amid ongoing US and Israeli operations in Iran, experts examine the military, regional, and geopolitical effects. The conflict has sparked Iranian retaliation, nuclear threats, and oil market shocks, with regional war risks escalating. Chinese President Xi is monitoring the situation from the sidelines, a position experts say Beijing prefers. The US-Iran conflict has potential impacts on the Middle East and global stability. The situation is being closely watched, with real-time coverage and updates on the ground. The conflict also raises questions about US military domination, particularly in relation to China, with some suggesting Iran's response has dispelled notions of US superiority. The situation remains volatile, with ongoing developments and potential long-term consequences.

stories.headline: A rush for critical minerals echoes oil extraction injustice as harms fall on world's most vulnerable, scientists warn
stories.summary: The global rush for critical minerals like lithium, cobalt, and nickel is echoing the injustices of oil extraction, harming vulnerable communities. A UN report found that the extraction of these minerals is deepening poverty and creating public health crises. The process requires massive amounts of water, with 2024's global lithium production needing 456 billion liters, equivalent to the annual domestic water needs of 62 million people in sub-Saharan Africa. The extraction and processing of these minerals also produce significant climate harms, including deforestation, emissions-intensive refining, and destruction of carbon-rich ecosystems. This undermines the goal of decarbonization, as the production of these minerals is contributing to environmental degradation and climate change. The report highlights the need to address the hidden costs of critical mineral mining in the transition to a green economy.

stories.headline: Xiaomi 17T and 17T Pro full specs and prices leak They're expected to become official very soon, perhaps even next month.
stories.summary: Xiaomi 17T and 17T Pro specifications and prices have leaked ahead of their expected launch in May or June. The Xiaomi 17T will reportedly cost €749 (~$877) for the 12GB/256GB model, featuring a MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra processor. The 17T Pro will be powered by the Dimensity 9500 chipset and offer additional features such as wireless charging and a 144Hz OLED screen. The leaked specs suggest the devices will be high-end, with the 17T Pro standing out due to its advanced features. Pricing for the 17T Pro has not been revealed. The leak provides comprehensive details about the upcoming devices, indicating they will be premium offerings from Xiaomi. The company is expected to officially announce the devices soon, with global availability to follow.

stories.headline: Apple’s next AI move could completely change iPhone photography Apple’s rumored iOS 27 AI tools could transform iPhone photography with generative editing, smarter enhancements and powerful Apple Intelligence integration.
stories.summary: Apple is developing a suite of AI-powered photo editing tools for iOS 27, set to release this fall. The tools, powered by Apple Intelligence, will allow iPhone users to automatically enhance image quality, expand backgrounds, and reframe shots after they're taken. The Photos app will feature a new "Apple Intelligence Tools" section, including tools such as Enhance, Extend, Reframe, and Clean Up. Enhance will use AI to improve color, lighting, and overall image quality. These features will also be available on iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. The update is expected to significantly transform iPhone photography, offering users more advanced and intuitive editing capabilities. The new tools are part of Apple's efforts to integrate AI technology into its operating systems, enhancing the overall user experience.

stories.headline: HONOR’s big reveal at Miss Universe PH 2026 Coronation Night? Leading global AI smart devices provider HONOR Philippines is once again making the unexpected happen as it teased a potential partnership
stories.summary: HONOR Philippines, a leading global AI smart devices provider, has teased a potential partnership with Miss Universe Philippines 2026. The company hinted at a new device launch during the pageant's coronation night on May 2, 2026. Fans speculate that the upcoming device could be the HONOR 600 Series. The teaser has generated excitement among fans, who are looking forward to the reveal. As a subsidiary of Chinese telecommunications giant Huawei, HONOR has established itself as a significant player in the mobile, tablet, and wearables market since its inception in 2013. The brand's latest mobile launch is the 600 series, and the upcoming launch is expected to generate significant interest. The partnership with Miss Universe Philippines 2026 is seen as a strategic move to increase brand visibility and reach a wider audience.

stories.headline: Why are the coolest girls you know are building cyberdecks? A hallmark of 80s hacker culture, the cyberdeck is being revived by a slew of hot girls. Why are so many turning back to analogue tech?
stories.summary: A resurgence of interest in cyberdecks, a hallmark of 80s hacker culture, is being driven by a group of individuals, particularly women. A cyberdeck is a small, custom-built computer with visible wires and memory boards, optimized for different uses. Each of the seven available cyberdecks has unique strengths, suited to various play styles, and becomes more effective at higher tiers. The Arasaka MK5 cyberdeck is particularly notable, transforming the Netrunner build into a top-tier option, but comes at a cost of 35,000 eddies. Cyberdecks are being built and used for their versatility and customization, with each one lending itself to a different approach. The trend of building and using cyberdecks is a shift towards analogue tech, with individuals seeking to create their own unique devices. This movement is driven by a desire for customization and control.

stories.headline: No. 1 overall recruit Tyran Stokes commits to Kansas
stories.summary: Tyran Stokes, the No. 1 overall recruit in the 2026 class, has committed to Kansas basketball. The nation's top prospect announced his decision on ESPN's "Inside the NBA." Stokes' commitment significantly upgrades Kansas' roster, which will be led by coach Bill Self, who announced his return for at least one more season nearly a month ago. Stokes chose Kansas over Kentucky, giving the Jayhawks the top-ranked high school prospect for the second consecutive year. The commitment was one of the last major announcements of the offseason, ending months of speculation about Stokes' future. With Stokes on board, Kansas' 2026 recruiting class has received a substantial boost, setting the stage for a promising season under Self's leadership. The announcement was highly anticipated, and Stokes' decision is expected to have a major impact on the college basketball landscape.

stories.headline: Afghan women's refugee team allowed to play in FIFA tournaments
stories.summary: The FIFA Council has approved amendments to its Governance Regulations, allowing the Afghan women's refugee team to compete in international soccer competitions. The team, known as Afghan Women United, was formed for female players who fled Afghanistan due to the Taliban rule. This decision provides an opportunity to ensure gender equity and human rights in sport. The team will be recognized as the official Afghanistan national team, enabling them to participate in FIFA tournaments. The regulation change was agreed upon by the FIFA Council in British Columbia, marking a significant milestone for the team and a step towards promoting human rights in sports. The decision comes five years after the national team players fled their country, and it will enable the team to compete against other national teams.

stories.headline: 'First breath in heaven': Ex-NFL defensive end Josh Mauro, 35, passes away
stories.summary: Former NFL defensive end Josh Mauro, 35, passed away on Thursday, April 23rd. His family announced his death, stating "Josh breathed his last breath on this earth and his first breath in heaven." Mauro played eight seasons in the NFL from 2014-2021, with stints with the Arizona Cardinals and Oakland Raiders. His former teams paid tribute to him, remembering him as an outstanding person who made an impact on and off the field. Mauro's family expressed gratitude for prayers and support during this difficult time, citing their faith as a source of strength. The cause of his death has not been disclosed. Mauro's NFL career spanned seven years, with his most recent season being in 2021. He is remembered for his contributions to the sport and his positive influence on those around him.

stories.headline: Arsenal, Atletico… and Reims? Ranking the ‘biggest’ clubs who have never won the Champions League
stories.summary: Arsenal and Atletico Madrid are among the biggest clubs to have never won the Champions League or its predecessor, the European Cup. Atlético Madrid has reached three finals without winning, while Arsenal has not appeared in a final. They are joined by Reims, who have finished as runners-up twice without winning. Spanish teams have dominated the competition, with Real Madrid and Barcelona winning 20 titles between them. Juventus has been runners-up the most times, losing seven finals. Arsenal and Atletico Madrid are currently competing in the semi-finals, with Arsenal facing Atletico Madrid in the first leg in Madrid. The two teams are seeking to win their first Champions League title, with Paris St-Germain having lifted the trophy for the first time last season.

stories.headline: ‘Hai dum?’: TMC MP's big challenge to PM Modi if Mamata wins in West Bengal
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Derek O'Brien challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to resign if Mamata Banerjee and the TMC win in the West Bengal Assembly elections. O'Brien's challenge came as the state voted in the second phase of polling on April 29. The TMC MP referred to Modi's earlier claim that he was the candidate for all 294 seats, and asked "Hai dum?" (do you have the courage?). O'Brien's statement was made in a video message, where he dared Modi to step down if the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is defeated by the Mamata Banerjee-led party. The West Bengal Assembly elections have concluded, and the results are awaited. O'Brien's challenge is seen as a confident assertion of the TMC's chances of winning the election. The outcome of the election will determine the fate of the challenge made by the TMC MP.

stories.headline: Preventive detentions only when absolutely necessary, act without bias: Calcutta High Court to ECI
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court has instructed electoral authorities in West Bengal to use preventive detention only when absolutely necessary. The court emphasized that such measures should be taken strictly according to law, considering the factor of personal liberty. A division bench comprising Chief Justice Sujoy Paul and Justice Partha Sarathi Sen cautioned against harassing individuals without prior records or proven charges of involvement in poll-related violence. The court's directive comes ahead of the final phase of polling in Bengal, underscoring the importance of following due process when curbing the fundamental right to liberty. The Election Commission of India was advised to act without bias and ensure that preventive detention or arrest is used only in essential cases, with the court disposing of a related petition. The ruling aims to balance the need for maintaining law and order with protecting individual rights.

stories.headline: 'Got the guts?' TMC's Derek O'Brien dares PM Modi to resign if TMC party retains Bengal
stories.summary: Trinamool Congress (TMC) Rajya Sabha MP Derek O'Brien has dared Prime Minister Narendra Modi to resign if the TMC wins the West Bengal state election. O'Brien made the challenge in a post on social media, saying Modi should step down as Prime Minister on May 4 if the TMC, led by Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, emerges victorious. He asked Modi if he has the "guts" to accept the challenge. The dare comes after the first phase of the West Bengal Assembly Elections saw a record-breaking 93% voter turnout. O'Brien's challenge is seen as a sharp swipe at the Prime Minister, who had earlier announced that he is a candidate for all 294 seats in the state. The TMC is seeking to retain power in the state, while the BJP is attempting to unseat them.

stories.headline: ‘How did game change?’: Raja Raghuvanshi’s family shocked after Sonam gets bail, cries manipulation
stories.summary: Raja Raghuvanshi's family is shocked after his wife Sonam was granted bail. The family plans to challenge the lower court's decision in the Meghalaya High Court, citing suspected manipulation in the investigation. Vipin Raghuvanshi, Raja's elder brother, claims the Meghalaya Police did not properly inform Sonam of the reason for her arrest, violating legal provisions. He also states that the prosecution has not provided him with a copy of the chargesheet, nor has he had a chance to review it properly. The family demands justice and is questioning how the case took a sudden turn after nine months of investigation. They will appeal the bail decision, seeking a thorough review of the case and the investigation process. The family's concerns highlight the complexity and potential irregularities in the case.

stories.headline: UAE quits OPEC in shock move, rattles global oil markets and challenges Saudi dominance Strategic exit amid Iran war weakens OPEC’s grip, opens door for higher UAE output, and reshapes global energy geopolitics
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has quit the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) in a surprise move, effective May 1. The decision reflects the UAE's long-term strategic and economic priorities, according to the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure. The exit comes after six decades of membership and is seen as a blow to OPEC and its de facto leader, Saudi Arabia. Tensions between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over oil output policy and regional influence have been building for years. UAE Energy Minister Suhail Mohamed al-Mazrouei stated that the decision was made after a careful review of the country's energy strategies, without consultation with other countries, including Saudi Arabia. The move is expected to weaken OPEC's grip on the global oil market and potentially lead to higher UAE oil output.

stories.headline: UAE's OPEC exit may not hit oil markets, say executives UAEs planned exit from OPEC is unlikely to disrupt global oil markets despite its sizable output, say industry executives, though it may deepen regional tension
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates' planned exit from OPEC and the OPEC+ alliance, effective May 1, 2026, is expected to have limited immediate impact on global oil markets. Despite the UAE's sizable oil output, industry executives believe the move will not disrupt oil markets. The decision follows a review of the UAE's production policy and future capacity, with the goal of maintaining a stable energy system that depends on flexible, reliable, and affordable supply. However, the exit may deepen regional tensions and reshape geopolitics in the Gulf. The UAE's withdrawal is set to take effect in May 2026, and its impact on global oil prices and markets is being closely watched by industry experts and analysts. The move is seen as a significant development in the global energy landscape.

stories.headline: Commentary: How Middle East Geopolitics Will Reshape China’s Export Engine Commentary: How Middle East Geopolitics Will Reshape China’s Export Engine - While prolonged blockades in the Middle East threaten global demand, China’s grip o
stories.summary: China's export engine is being reshaped by Middle East geopolitics, with prolonged blockades threatening global demand. Despite this, China's exports of solar capacity reached a record high of 68GW in the first month of the Iran crisis. China dominates supply chains for clean energy technologies, including wind turbines, solar panels, and batteries. The country's biggest export products by value in 2025 were phone devices, electronic integrated circuits, computers, cars, and electric storage batteries. China's exports are also impacted by tariffs, taxes, and geopolitics in other regions, such as Russia, where the auto boom has cooled. The Middle East conflict has rippled through China's chemical markets, and the country's exports by country are tracked by the United Nations COMTRADE database, with Europe and the Middle East being key regions. China's export statistics are updated regularly.

stories.headline: UAE’s OPEC Exit May not Hit Oil Market: Executives The UAEs exit from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is likely to have greater implications for geopolitics in the Persian Gulf than
stories.summary: The UAE's exit from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is unlikely to disrupt global oil markets despite its sizable output. The UAE, OPEC's third-largest producer, accounted for roughly 12 percent of the organization's total output. Industry executives believe the exit will have greater implications for geopolitics in the Persian Gulf, potentially deepening regional tensions and reshaping the region's dynamics. The UAE's departure from OPEC and OPEC+ is set to take effect on May 1. The move has exposed long-running tensions between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over oil production limits and geopolitics. The UAE joined OPEC in 1967 and has been a member for over five decades, making its departure a significant development for the organization. Experts will be watching for potential impacts on global oil prices and supply risks.

stories.headline: Sensex rises 950 pts, Nifty near 24,300; Positive Q4 earnings among key factors behind market rally
stories.summary: The Sensex rose 950 points, with the Nifty nearing 24,300, driven by positive Q4 earnings among other key factors. Banking shares, including Axis Bank and AU Small Finance Bank, led the uptrend, with the Bank Nifty recovering from previous losses. A favourable union budget and potential trade agreement with the US are expected to trigger market growth after consolidation in 2025. The Nifty may consolidate within the range of 24,500-23,400, according to ICICI Direct, as it navigates geopolitical volatility and reacts to ongoing corporate earnings. Earlier, the Sensex had soared 1,000 points, with the Nifty above 24,300, before erasing some gains to trade below 24,200. Strong buying interest in banking and other sectors contributed to the market rally, with Sun Pharma also rallying 7% in recent trading sessions.

stories.headline: Sensex rises 400 points, Nifty nears 24,100 amid fresh hopes for Iran-US war de-escalation
stories.summary: The Sensex rose nearly 400 points, with the Nifty nearing 24,100, amid fresh hopes for de-escalation of the Iran-US war. US President Donald Trump stated that the conflict with Iran could end soon, and a 10-day ceasefire has been agreed upon between Lebanon and Israel, a key condition set by Iran. The stock market reacted positively to the easing of Iran tensions, with the Sensex jumping 359 points and the Nifty approaching 24,100. Additionally, a sharper-than-expected fall in retail inflation to a six-year low in April also boosted investor sentiment. The BSE Sensex was up 462 points at 81,610, while the NSE Nifty50 rose 135 points to 24,713, driven by positive global cues and easing geopolitical tensions. The market gains were led by a rebound in IT, financial, and pharma stocks.

stories.headline: Stock Market Today Live: Stock to buy today: Triveni Engineering & Industries (₹405.70) Sensex Today, Nifty 50 | Stock Market Live Updates
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a decline, with the Nifty50 closing below 24,000 and the Sensex down 983 points. This downturn is attributed to rising crude oil prices and the ongoing US-Iran impasse. The BSE and NSE will reopen on April 27, 2026. Triveni Engineering & Industries is highlighted as a stock to consider, currently priced at ₹405.70. The Nifty50 Index chart shows the latest index dynamics, with resources available for tracking candlestick and periodic charts, as well as forecasts and market news. Investors can access live updates, share prices, and top gainers and losers through various finance sites, including Angel One and Groww Terminal. The current market situation is being closely monitored, with crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions being key factors influencing the market's performance.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Today: Sensex, Nifty rebound in early trade, supported by DII buying and Asian markets
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 rebounded in early trade, supported by gains in blue-chip stocks and a positive trend in Asian markets. Domestic institutional investor (DII) buying also offered support to the markets. The rebound comes after a previous surge, where the Sensex jumped nearly 1900 points and the Nifty rose 2.5%. Analysts remain structurally optimistic about the markets' outlook for the next fiscal year, anticipating a recovery once geopolitical tensions subside and crude oil prices stabilize. The Indian equity markets have shown resilience, rebounding from early losses due to sustained investor inflows and positive global cues. The current trend indicates a positive start to the trading day, with the Sensex and Nifty trading higher.

stories.headline: UAE OPEC exit is not without precedence. Who could be next?
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced its withdrawal from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and OPEC+, effective May 1, 2026. The UAE joined OPEC in 1967 and has been a member since the country's formation in 1971. The exit is attributed to long-running tensions between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over oil production limits and geopolitics. This move poses a significant existential crisis for OPEC, according to Javier Blas, the biggest since the group's establishment over half a century ago. The UAE's departure is seen as the end of Gulf solidarity rather than just an issue about oil. Its exit is not without precedence, raising questions about which country could be next to leave the cartel. The UAE's withdrawal marks a significant shift in the dynamics of the oil-producing nations.

stories.headline: The race to mine critical minerals for AI and clean energy is creating ‘sacrifice zones’ that harm water and health of world’s poor
stories.summary: The extraction of critical minerals, such as lithium and cobalt, necessary for AI and clean energy technologies, is resulting in 'sacrifice zones' that harm the water and health of impoverished communities. Mining operations for these minerals require vast amounts of water, often in water-scarce regions, with lithium mining consuming approximately 1.9 million liters of water per metric ton produced. The global rush to secure these minerals is driven by the need to meet climate goals and advance digital technologies. Countries, including the US, are prioritizing access to these minerals, with potential mining deals in places like Greenland and Ukraine. The high demand for critical minerals is threatening the health and well-being of vulnerable populations, highlighting the need for sustainable and responsible mining practices. The environmental and social impacts of mining are undermining the promise of a sustainable transition.

stories.headline: Questions asked about power price rises Power prices are rising, but how much - and how do you get a better deal?
stories.summary: Power prices are rising due to the soaring cost of natural gas, which generates over 40% of electricity. As more gas is exported, utilities face higher prices. The energy price cap, which changes quarterly, can lead to price fluctuations. Fixed-price deals offer certainty for a set period but may result in higher prices if energy costs drop. The market price cap limits spot electricity prices to $18,600 per megawatt hour. In Ontario, the system is organized by retailers and generators, with rates set by the Ontario Energy Board. The rising cost of natural gas and decreased generator supply contribute to price increases. To get a better deal, consumers can explore fixed-price deals or shop around with retailers. Understanding the drivers of price rises and their impact on different customers and regions is crucial for managing energy costs. The Ontario Energy Board plays a key role in regulating the industry.

stories.headline: WA farmers seeding their 'riskiest crop in years' welcome early rain
stories.summary: Western Australian farmers are seeding their riskiest crop in years due to geopolitical tensions and uncertainty. The region is expecting a window of rain this week, which is welcomed by farmers. However, concerns remain about fuel supplies for the 2026-27 harvest later in the season. Meanwhile, farmers in two Australian states are battling a potential mouse plague, reminiscent of the 2020 and 2021 plagues that ravaged farms and rural communities on the east coast. The early rain brings hope, but the dry season is expected to start soon, adding to the challenges faced by farmers. The combination of weather and geopolitical factors is making this season particularly challenging for growers, who are bracing for a potentially difficult harvest. Fuel supply concerns are also a major worry for the upcoming season.

stories.headline: Google employee says he is ashamed of the company due to its secret military AI work
stories.summary: Google has signed a Pentagon defense deal to use its AI models for classified tasks, sparking outrage among employees. Andreas Kirsch, a research scientist at Google DeepMind, expressed shame over the agreement, stating he was "incredibly ashamed" and "speechless". Google defended the deal, saying it is an amendment to an existing contract and will support logistics and cybersecurity. The company had previously signed a deal for unclassified use of its AI systems. Employees are warning against classified military AI work, citing concerns over the company's reputation and ethics. A petition has been started, urging CEO Sundar Pichai to refuse classified military AI work with the Pentagon. The controversy comes as Google is also "updating" its diversity and inclusion employee training programs, according to its former head of diversity, Melonie Parker.

stories.headline: US Stock Market: OpenAI growth concerns spark broad selloff in AI-linked stocks
stories.summary: A broad selloff occurred in artificial intelligence-linked stocks after a report indicated OpenAI failed to meet key sales and user growth targets. This sparked concerns about the returns on massive investments in the technology. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq declined as a result. Nvidia and other chip stocks fell, with Nvidia closing in the red. Companies with ties to OpenAI, such as Oracle and CoreWeave, saw significant declines, with Oracle ending 4.1% lower and CoreWeave falling 5.8%. Microsoft, a larger partner of OpenAI, initially reversed losses but was affected by the overall market sentiment. The AI sentiment score was 28/100, indicating a bearish outlook. The report dragged down stocks of companies that have invested in or partnered with OpenAI, pausing the AI rally and sparking profit-taking in the semiconductor sector.

stories.headline: Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman head to court in high-stakes showdown over AI
stories.summary: Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman are heading to court in a high-stakes trial starting April 27. The lawsuit, filed by Musk, alleges betrayal and deceit, and seeks Altman's removal from OpenAI's board. The dispute stems from a bitter falling out between the former allies after Musk stopped funding the company. The trial's outcome has significant implications for OpenAI, which plans to go public later this year with a valuation of around $1 trillion. Musk is seeking the return of "ill-gotten gains" to OpenAI's nonprofit, rather than personal compensation. Jury selection will begin in a federal courthouse in Oakland, near OpenAI's San Francisco headquarters. The case revolves around OpenAI's founding mission and the alleged actions of Altman, with Musk aiming to restore the company's original purpose. The trial is expected to be closely watched due to its potential impact on the AI industry.

stories.headline: Elon Musk takes stand in trial vs. Sam Altman that could reshape AI’s future
stories.summary: Elon Musk, Tesla CEO and OpenAI cofounder, took the stand in a high-stakes trial against Sam Altman, OpenAI's CEO, in an Oakland, California federal court. The trial revolves around a bitter feud between Musk and Altman, which could reshape the future of artificial intelligence. Musk, who split from OpenAI years after cofounding it as a nonprofit, claimed the AI startup was prioritizing commercial interests. A nine-person jury was seated on Monday, and the trial began with Musk's testimony. The case involves a lawsuit filed by Musk against Altman and OpenAI, with the outcome potentially impacting the development of AI, including OpenAI's ChatGPT chatbot. The trial is a culmination of a long-standing rivalry between two tech industry leaders, formerly friends, now turned rivals.
